slides.title: Cover — ReconPro
slides.task_brief: Cover slide with full OLED black background. Center-aligned content. Top: small gold badge 'ENTERPRISE ATTACK SURFACE MANAGEMENT'. Center: Large bold 'ReconPro' in white (72px). Below: tagline 'See everything. Protect everything.' in muted gray. Bottom: version 'v0.2.0 — August 2026' in mono micro text. Gold accent line above the tagline. slides.title: The Problem
slides.task_brief: Left column (60%): Section label 'THE PROBLEM' in gold mono small. Large heading 'Attack surfaces are exploding' in white 36px. Body text (18px, #999): 'Organizations deploy hundreds of services, APIs, and cloud resources. Each one expands the attack surface. Security teams lack real-time visibility into what they own, what is exposed, and what is vulnerable. Traditional tools scan once and forget. By the time a report is generated, the landscape has already changed.' Right column (40%): Three stacked stat cards with large numbers — '6,000+' labeled 'New CVEs per year' (danger red), '68%' labeled 'Of breaches involve unpatched vulns' (gold), '$4.45M' labeled 'Average breach cost 2023' (red). Dark card backgrounds with 1px border.

slides.title: The Solution — ReconPro
slides.task_brief: Section label 'THE SOLUTION' in gold mono small. Large heading 'Continuous attack surface intelligence' in white 36px. Subheading 'ReconPro monitors, scans, and protects your entire digital footprint in real-time.' in #999. Three feature cards in a row below: Card 1 — icon radar, title 'Real-Time Scanning', body '15 scanner modules continuously monitor DNS, ports, SSL, headers, and more.' Card 2 — icon shield, title 'Threat Detection', body 'Automated vulnerability identification with risk scoring and remediation guidance.' Card 3 — icon chart, title 'Compliance Engine', body 'SOC2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, GDPR compliance reports generated automatically.' Gold border-top on each card. Speaker notes: Emphasize continuous vs point-in-time.

slides.title: Architecture Overview
slides.task_brief: Section label 'ARCHITECTURE' in gold mono small. Heading 'Built for scale, designed for security' in white. 2x3 bento grid of architecture components: (1) 'Scanner Engine' — '15 modules: DNS, subdomain, HTTP, port, SSL, cert, CT logs, WHOIS, email, geo, directory, network, log, process, file' (2) 'API Layer' — '54 RESTful endpoints with API key auth, rate limiting, and SSRF protection' (3) 'Database' — '21 Prisma models with SQLite/PostgreSQL, full referential integrity, 15+ indexes' (4) 'Frontend' — 'Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript strict, Tailwind CSS 4, 26 active components' (5) 'Security' — 'bcrypt hashing, HttpOnly sessions, CSP nonces, HSTS 1yr, COOP/CORP/COEP' (6) 'Infrastructure' — 'Docker, K8s, systemd, Nginx TLS, Railway, Render, Fly.io ready'. Each card has dark bg, gold accent on top border. Speaker notes: highlight that this is production-ready, not a prototype.

slides.title: Technology Stack
slides.task_brief: Section label 'TECHNOLOGY' in gold mono small. Heading 'Modern stack, enterprise grade' in white. Two columns. Left: 'Frontend & API' with items: Next.js 16.1 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript (strict mode), Tailwind CSS 4, Prisma 6.11 ORM, Framer Motion animations, Radix UI components. Right: 'Security & Infrastructure' with items: bcryptjs password hashing, Ed25519 cryptographic attestations, SHA-256 API key hashing, SSRF guard (IPv4 + IPv6), Content Security Policy with nonces, Docker multi-stage builds, Kubernetes manifests. Each item on a row with a small green dot bullet. Mono font for version numbers. Speaker notes: emphasize that all dependencies are actively maintained and industry-standard.

slides.title: Key Features — Scanner Engine
slides.task_brief: Section label 'SCANNER ENGINE' in gold mono small. Heading '15 scanner modules. One unified view.' in white. Grid of scanner capabilities in 3 columns with 5 rows each: DNS Enumeration, Subdomain Discovery, HTTP Header Analysis, Port Scanning, SSL/TLS Validation, Certificate Transparency, WHOIS Intelligence, Email Recon, Geolocation Mapping, Directory Brute Force, Network Interfaces, Log Analysis, Process Scanner, File System Audit, Registry Analysis. Each as a small card with gold text and mono label. Below: a wide card with 'Scan Types' showing 4 badges: 'Full Scan' 'Quick Scan' 'Stealth Scan' 'Compliance Scan'. Speaker notes: emphasize these are real scanners making real network calls, not simulated.

slides.title: Security Architecture
slides.task_brief: Section label 'SECURITY' in gold mono small. Heading 'Defense in depth, by design' in white. Left column (55%): Stacked security features with gold icons and descriptions: 'Password Security — bcrypt with 12 rounds, per-user salted hashes', 'Session Management — Server-side sessions, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax cookies', 'SSRF Protection — Private IP rejection, DNS validation, redirect blocking', 'Rate Limiting — Configurable per-IP limits on all endpoints', 'CSP Headers — Nonce-based Content Security Policy on all pages', 'HSTS — 1-year max-age with includeSubDomains and preload'. Right column (45%): A security badge graphic — concentric circles representing defense layers, with labels: Perimeter (Nginx/TLS), Application (CSP/Headers), API (Auth/Rate Limit), Data (Encrypted at rest). Use CSS-drawn circles with gold/blue borders. Speaker notes: This is not theoretical — all protections are active and tested.

slides.title: Market & Business Model
slides.task_brief: Section label 'MARKET' in gold mono small. Heading 'A massive and growing market' in white. Top row — 3 stat cards: '$18.3B' labeled 'Attack surface management market by 2028' (gold), '27%' labeled 'CAGR 2023-2028' (green), '94%' labeled 'Of enterprises have multi-cloud environments' (blue). Bottom section — two columns: Left 'Target Customers': 'Enterprise security teams', 'Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs)', 'DevSecOps teams', 'Compliance officers'. Right 'Revenue Model': 'SaaS subscription (monthly/annual)', 'Per-organization pricing', 'Tiered plans: Starter / Professional / Enterprise', 'Add-ons: Advanced scanning, custom reports'. slides.title: Competitive Advantage
slides.task_brief: Section label 'COMPETITIVE EDGE' in gold mono small. Heading 'Why ReconPro wins' in white. Comparison table with 3 columns: Feature (left), ReconPro (center, highlighted with gold border-top), Legacy Tools (right). Rows: 'Scanning Frequency' — 'Continuous' vs 'Point-in-time'; 'Scanner Modules' — '15 modules' vs '3-5 modules'; 'Real-Time Updates' — 'SSE streaming' vs 'Poll-based'; 'Compliance Reports' — '5 frameworks' vs 'Manual'; 'Deployment' — 'Cloud or Self-hosted' vs 'Cloud only'; 'API Access' — '54 endpoints' vs 'Limited REST'; 'Price' — 'Fraction of cost' vs '$50K+/year'. ReconPro column cells are highlighted with subtle gold background. Speaker notes: ReconPro delivers more at a fraction of the cost.

slides.title: Product Roadmap
slides.task_brief: Section label 'ROADMAP' in gold mono small. Heading 'From strength to strength' in white. Timeline with 4 phases as horizontal cards: 'Q3 2026 (v0.2.0 — Current)' — 'Production launch, 15 scanner modules, team management, compliance engine, enterprise security architecture' (green badge: 'SHIPPED'). 'Q4 2026 (v0.3.0)' — 'MFA support, email verification, enhanced scanning (WAF fingerprint, JS analysis), API pagination, advanced reporting' (gold badge: 'IN PROGRESS'). Speaker notes: We have a clear, achievable product roadmap.

slides.title: Demo & Deployment
slides.task_brief: Section label 'DEPLOYMENT' in gold mono small. Heading 'Deploy in minutes. Anywhere.' in white. Body: 'ReconPro runs on any infrastructure — from a single Docker container to a full Kubernetes cluster. One command to deploy. Zero external dependencies required for the default SQLite configuration.' Below: Grid of deployment targets as icon cards — 'Docker' 'Railway' 'Render' 'Fly.io' 'AWS EC2' 'Azure VM' 'GCP' 'DigitalOcean' 'VPS (Ubuntu)' 'Kubernetes' 'Coolify' — each as a small dark card with gold text. Below: a terminal-style code block showing 'docker compose up -d' with a green success prompt. Speaker notes: Emphasize how easy it is to get started — literally one command.
